literal: She of tight bangles having practiced exceeding feigned-indifference, intense-grief curing remedy one possesses.
translation: The excessive, feigned indifference shown by her who wears tight-fitting bangles contains within itself a remedy to cure the very grief it causes.
modern: நெருக்கமான வளையல்களை அணிந்தவள் எல்லை கடந்து செய்த பொய்க் கோபம், அதனால் உண்டாகும் மிகுந்த துன்பத்தைத் தீர்க்கும் ஒரு மருந்தையும் தன்னுள் கொண்டுள்ளது.
explanation: In this couplet, the lover speaks of his beloved's playful avoidance or feigned anger, referred to as 'kaḷḷam' (deceit or pretense). She is described as wearing tight-fitting bangles ('ceṟitoṭi'), and her mock indifference has exceeded normal limits. Although this behavior causes him intense grief ('uṟutuyar'), he realizes that her playful pretense actually contains the remedy ('maruntu') to cure his distress. The remedy is her underlying love, which will soon reveal itself and bring him joy.
